procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires factories to complete Factory Registration on its portal as a prerequisite prior to applying for a certificate of origin, taking about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides an e-service for exporters and local manufacturers to submit applications for Certificates of Origin for India with required documents.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate of origin fee ranging from AED 10 to AED 200 based on the shipment invoice value in AED.
The competent authority issues the Certificate of Origin prior to, at, or within 5 working days of export, valid for 12 months for a single import shipment.

The Indian importer claims preferential duty rates upon filing the bill of entry, maintains origin records for at least 5 years, and reportedly uploads electronic certificates via e-Sanchit (unconfirmed).
The exporter must retain all origin records, including cost breakdowns, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the year of certificate issuance.

caveats.note: CEPA preferential rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and safeguard or anti-dumping duties still apply.
Mansha interprets '+' in origin rules as requiring both tests (change in tariff sub-heading and value addition) to pass, as the agreement does not explicitly define '+'.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
